# Releases a maintenance version of openmrs-core from a maintenance branch (N.N.x).
#
# This duplicates the manual "Release" stage (and the "Release image variants" stage that
# follows it automatically) of the Bamboo plan defined in bamboo-specs/bamboo.yml
# (e.g. TRUNK-OC28 "OpenMRS Core 2.8.x").
# For example, dispatching it on 2.8.x with releaseVersion=2.8.8 will:
#   1. set the maven version to 2.8.8 and commit "[skip-ci] [skip actions] Releasing 2.8.8"
#      as openmrs-bot ([skip-ci] is Bamboo's skip marker; [skip actions] is the one GitHub
#      recognizes, so the release commit does not trigger a redundant CI run)
#   2. build and push openmrs/openmrs-core:2.8.8-dev and :2.8.8 (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64)
#   3. deploy the release artifacts to the OpenMRS Nexus releases repository by running
#      mvn deploy inside the :2.8.8-dev image, exactly as Bamboo does
#   4. tag 2.8.8 and push the tag
#   5. push the release commit to 2.8.x, then set the next development version
#      (auto-incremented to 2.8.9-SNAPSHOT, or the developmentVersion input if given)
#      and push "Setting new SNAPSHOT version" (non-fatal, as in Bamboo)
#   6. build and push the per-JDK image variants from the tag:
#      openmrs/openmrs-core:2.8.8[-dev]-amazoncorretto-{8,11,17,21}
#
# Required secrets:
#   OMRS_RELEASE_BOT_APP_ID / OMRS_RELEASE_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY
#                                               org-level secrets already shared with this
#                                               repo; preferred token source (short-lived App
#                                               installation tokens, like the shared module
#                                               release workflow). REQUIRED SETUP: the App
#                                               must be added as a bypass actor on each
#                                               maintenance-branch ruleset — the validation
#                                               pre-flight can only verify the token
#                                               authenticates and the branch state, NOT
#                                               ruleset bypass (git push --dry-run never runs
#                                               server-side rules), so without the bypass the
#                                               branch push is rejected only after the maven

### Compile Stage (platform-agnostic)
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM maven:3.9-$DEV_JDK AS compile

WORKDIR /openmrs_core

COPY docker-pom.xml .

rows.title: TRUNK-6512: Introduce ConceptReferenceRangeContext API
rows.excerpt:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **dkayiwa** · [Slack thread](https://openmrs.slack.com/archives/C021QUDSD5K/p1788308814384069)_

## Description of what I changed

This is a backport of TRUNK-6512 to the `2.7.x` maintenance branch. It is ported from the current state of `2.8.x` rather than cherry-picked from the original 2.7.x commit, because that commit (`f127132c`) was written against the old Velocity-based criteria utility, which TRUNK-6610 has since replaced with SpEL on this branch.

**Before:** resolving a concept reference range on 2.7.x means going through an `Obs`. `ConceptService.getConceptReferenceRange(Person, Concept)` fabricates a throwaway `new Obs(person, concept, null, null)` and hands it to `new ObsValidator().getReferenceRange(obs)`, and the whole selection algorithm — evaluating each range's criteria, falling back to the `ConceptNumeric`'s own bounds, and merging multiple matches into the strictest range — lives inside the validator. A caller that only has a person and a concept, or that wants ranges evaluated as of some date other than today (retrospective data entry, for instance), has no way to say so: the criteria are always evaluated against a synthetic Obs with a null `obsDatetime`.

**After:** there is a first-class `ConceptReferenceRangeContext` that carries the person, the concept, an optional evaluation date, and — when it was built from one — the originating `Obs` and `Encounter`. `ConceptService.getConceptReferenceRange(ConceptReferenceRangeContext)` resolves a range from that context, and the selection algorithm now lives in `ConceptServiceImpl` where the rest of the concept logic is, instead of in a validator. Criteria expressions can use `$context` alongside the existing `$patient`, `$obs`, `$encounter`, `$date`, and `$fn`, and `$date` now reflects the context's date rather than always coming from an Obs.

## How

- New `api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/ConceptReferenceRangeContext.java`, with constructors for `(Person, Concept, Date)`, `(Obs)`, and `(Encounter, Concept)`.
- `ConceptService`/`ConceptServiceImpl` gain the `ConceptReferenceRangeContext` overload; `ConceptReferenceRangeUtility` gains `evaluateCriteria(String, ConceptReferenceRangeContext)`.
- The existing `evaluateCriteria(String, Obs)` and `getConceptReferenceRange(Person, Concept)` signatures are kept and now delegate to the context-based versions,

rows.title: maven(deps): bump org.owasp.encoder:encoder from 1.4.1 to 1.5.0
rows.excerpt:
Bumps [org.owasp.encoder:encoder](https://github.com/OWASP/owasp-java-encoder) from 1.4.1 to 1.5.0.
Release notes

Sourced from org.owasp.encoder:encoder's releases.

OWASP Java Encoder 1.5.0

Version 1.5.0 is available from Maven Central. All nine binary/source/Javadoc JARs, four POMs, and their thirteen signatures were downloaded from Central and verified against the retained signed release files. There is no encoder-esapi:1.5.0 release.

Security and correctness

  • Fixes encoded fragments completing outer HTML or XML parser delimiters across trusted-text boundaries in JavaScript HTML/block, CDATA, and XML-comment contexts. Versions through 1.4.1 are affected. See GHSA-g8p6-7r8f-qrpv.
  • Fixes EncodedWriter close/finalization behavior, exception handling, and overflow-safe array-slice validation.
  • Adds JSON encoding APIs and matching JSP/Jakarta tags and EL functions, plus XML 1.1 bindings.

Compatibility and migration

Public Java APIs remain binary and source compatible with 1.4.1 for the three supported libraries. Java 8 remains the minimum runtime; packaged consumers passed on Java 8, 11, 17, 21, and 25.

The security fixes deliberately change some encoded output:

  • JavaScript HTML/block modes emit additional hexadecimal escapes while preserving the string value. Review byte snapshots, cache keys, signatures, and output-size budgets.
  • CDATA preserves parsed text but can expand to 13 output characters per input character and can change parser event boundaries.
  • XML-comment hyphens become ~ under the documented lossy policy.

The optional ESAPI adapter is retired. Version 1.4.1 is its final published release and is unsupported; migrate to direct Java Encoder APIs. Mixing the 1.4.1 adapter with the 1.5 core is not a supported migration.

See the migration notes,
